raw_response:
I've been working this land for 40 years. My body isn't what it was, and two of my children are away working in the city, so I can't rely on as much help as I used to. But I know this land. I know what it needs.

My 5 mu grows wheat in the cold months and maize in the hot months — same land, both crops, same as always. I won't change that. This rotation is what keeps the soil decent and gives me two harvests a year to live on.

For wheat this winter, I'll plant the same improved variety I've been buying from the village seed shop for years. I trust it. I'll do rotary tillage before planting — I hire someone with a machine for that. I'll put down base fertilizer before planting, then topdress at jointing. I water three times: once before winter sets in, once when the stalks are shooting up, once when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for weeds early on, once for rust or aphids if I see them.

For maize in summer, I'll plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest. No point wasting days. My son can help those few days. I'll apply fertilizer at planting and again at the big bell stage. I only water twice — once at planting if the soil is dry, once at silking. I spray once or twice depending on what I see with the pests. I use rotary tillage lightly before planting.

I won't push yields beyond what I can manage. Doing too much and making mistakes costs more than doing a bit less carefully.
